questions_and_answers.question_text: What kind of verb is liúxíng, and how is it made negative?
What does liúxíng mean with a phrase following it?
What do yǒu zhīshi, yǒu dàolǐ, and yǒu bāngzhu literally mean?
How do yǒu xìngqù and yǒu yìsi differ?
Write the Chinese for "It is popular to wear long skirts now."
Write the Chinese for "He has a very high position."
Name two other yǒu + noun adjectival verbs you have learned.

answers.answer_text: Any two of: yǒu guānxi ("to be related to"), yǒu yánjiū ("to be expert"), yǒu míng ("to be famous"), yǒu yòng ("to be useful").

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "They want independent economic and social status."

answers.answer_text: Tāmen yào yǒu dúlìde jīngjì hé shèhuì dìwèi.

articles.text:
10. A: Tā xiěde jǐběn xiǎoshuō      The novels he wrote are all very
       xiànzài dōu hěn liúxíng.      popular now.
    B: Nà dāngrán, xiàng tā nèiyàng Of course. Novels written by someone
       yǒu dìwèi yǒu zhīshide rén,   with his position and knowledge are
       xiěde xiǎoshuō yídìng yǒu     sure to be interesting.
       yìsi.

11. yǒu bāngzhu                    to be helpful
12. yǒu dàolǐ                      to make sense

Notes on Nos. 10 through 12

liúxíng: "to be popular, prevalent, current, widespread, common." This is an ADJECTIVAL VERB. Make it negative with bù.

Zhèizhǒng huà xiànzài hěn        This kind of talk is very popular
liúxíng, kěshi wǒ xiǎng zhè      these days, but I don't think it's
huà bú tài duì.                  very true.

You can also use liúxíng with a phrase following it to mean "to be popular TO (do something)":

Xiànzài liúxíng chuān cháng      It is popular to wear long skirts now.
qúnzi.
Zài hěn duō dìfang, yuè lái yuè  In a lot of places, it is getting more
liúxíng nánnǚ tóngjū le.         and more common for men and women to
                                 live together.

Liúxíng is also used in compound nouns, such as liúxíngbìng, "epidemic."

dìwèi: "position, place or status (in an organization or society)"

Tāde dìwèi hěn gāo.              He has a very high position.
Tāmen yào yǒu dúlìde jīngjì hé   They want independent economic and
shèhuì dìwèi.                    social status.

yǒu zhīshi: "to be knowledgeable," literally "to have knowledge"
yǒu dàolǐ: "to make sense," literally "to have reason"
yǒu bāngzhu: "to be helpful," literally "to have help"

Here you see three more examples of how yǒu and a noun can be used to make an ADJECTIVAL VERB. Sometimes the meaning of the resulting phrase is MORE than just the sum of its parts. Yǒu xìngqù is "to be interested (in something)," while yǒu yìsi is "to be interesting."

Here are some of the others you have already learned:

yǒu guānxi     to be related to      yǒu míng      to be famous
yǒu yánjiū     to be expert          yǒu yòng      to be useful
